findings.summary: §1.3 / §2 criterion 4 undelivered: the drain failure checker only matches the literal journal marker `[bash 非零退出 EXIT:<n>]`. The exact failure mode the package targets — a tick killed by the engine with `exec_failed` / `status=TIMEOUT`, whose journal result is verbatim `[外部调用失败 status=TIMEOUT]` (GT-15/GT-13) — matches no pattern here, so it is still swallowed and the drain still reports merely 'not yet converged'. The emitted line also carries only run_dir and exit=<n>, never the `status`, which §2 criterion 4b explicitly requires.

§2 criterion 4 has no discriminative test. g15-drain-failure-visible.test.ts (Y1/Y3) only writes journals containing `[bash 非零退出 EXIT:2]` — the pre-existing G15 behavior. No test constructs a tick that died with exec_failed/`status=TIMEOUT` and asserts the entry fails loudly naming run_dir, and no reverse case shows that treating it as 'not yet converged' turns the test red.

§2 criterion 4b regression violated: `MAX_CLUES` is not declared by the regression profile. The identifiers MAX_CLUES / --max-clues / max_clues do not occur anywhere in bin/, profiles/, src/ or workflows/; e0-regression.env declares MAX_WRITES=96 and TRIAGE_THRESHOLD=1 but no clue cap, and nothing narrows the regression research scope. This also leaves §2 criterion 6 self-inconsistent: the profile still declares DRAIN_WALL_CLOCK_SECONDS=2400 while the board runs to the default maxClues=64, i.e. the ~3-hour convergence the spec calls out is not narrowed as required.

§2 criterion 2b test is vacuous and non-discriminative. GT-16a/GT-16b stub every fetch with instant canned responses, so the measured `elapsed` is sub-millisecond by construction and `expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(15_000)` can never go red for any real timing regression — every latency source the criterion names (process/dependency startup, bus I/O, CAS, spawn, waiting for worker results, harvest, triage) is removed by the stub. It also does not drive a real `--run` on a seed board (the repo's test/fixtures/fake-bus.mjs harness, used by e0c2-termination.test.ts, is available for exactly this), and it hardcodes the literal 15_000 instead of deriving the bound from the engine-effective `limits.node_timeout` in workflows/deep-research/tick/workflow.yaml, which §2 criterion 2b explicitly demands. Reverting the fix would leave this test green.

§0 must-preserve item '耗时分阶段 timings' and the §1.1b evidence it backs are absent: no `timings` instrumentation exists anywhere in the delivery, so no phase-split measured numbers identify where a tick's time is spent. No E0c5-era marker appears in any product file, indicating the prior version's preserved-by-mandate work was not carried forward.

§2 criterion 2's discriminativeness is only half-real on the generate side. GT-17a fabricates the failure by injecting a generateDeps.spawnRole stub that throws GenerateWorkerExitedWithoutResultError directly, so it exercises the catch-and-continue at tick-run.ts:1751-1757 but never the actual detection path (checkRunExited inside readBody at tick-run.ts:1382-1385). No test constructs a real generate run that exited without a dr-doc.result.v1 and lets the production code raise the error; only the triage path (GT-14a) is genuinely driven.

GT-14b asserts only on a directly constructed TriageWorkerExitedWithoutResultError's name and message text; it drives no production code path and adds no discriminative value beyond what GT-14a already covers.

Correctly delivered and verified: §1.1's record-and-continue (generateError is threaded into RunWriteOutcome and surfaced by `--run`, which JSON-serializes the outcome to stdout and returns 0, so the diagnostic is greppable and the tick survives), the §1.1 boundary case (non-recognized errors still rethrow, GT-17b), and §1.2's triage-side short-circuit via checkRunExited on agent.run.exited.v1 with GT-14a/GT-14c forming a genuine red/green pair.
